references.text: The Lord appears to Abram and promises the land of Canaan to his descendants – the first land promise to Abraham.
God promises Abram all the land he can see, to him and his descendants forever – an expansion of the land promise.
The Lord makes a covenant with Abram and defines the borders of the land from the river of Egypt to the Euphrates.
God renews the land promise to Isaac and confirms the oath He swore to Abraham, including the promise of the land.
God renews the land promise to Jacob in his dream at Bethel, confirming that the land will be given to him and his descendants.
God says, 'I will take you as my people and I will be your God' – a direct parallel to the covenant formula 'I will be your God'.
The Lord shows Moses the promised land and reminds Him of the oath to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob to give it to their descendants.
Jeremiah proclaims the new covenant where God says, 'I will be their God, and they shall be my people' – a repetition of the covenant formula.
Paul explains that the promises were given to Abraham and his offspring, who is Christ, offering a christological interpretation of the land promise.
Abraham lived as a stranger in the promised land, trusting that God would fulfill the promise – a direct link to 'the land where you live as a foreigner'.
Ezekiel 36:28 confirms and completes Abraham's covenant by restoring the 'God-people' relationship and settlement in the land after exile.
Psalm 105:11 is a direct reference to and confirmation of God's promise of the land of Canaan given to Abraham in Genesis 17:8.
Genesis 26:3 confirms that Abraham's covenant (land and God's presence) remains valid for Isaac and his descendants.
Exodus 6:4 links the exodus from Egypt directly back to Abraham's covenant regarding the land as foreigners.
1 Chronicles 16:18 is a liturgical affirmation of Abraham's land promise as a central part of God's covenant history.
Leviticus 20:24 resumes the Abrahamic covenant formula (the land and 'I am your God') as the basis for Israel's life in the land.
Jeremiah 7:7 confirms that Abraham's promise of eternal settlement in the land remains valid even after judgment.
Numbers 34:2 is the concrete fulfillment of Abraham's general promise of Canaan as an inheritance.
Genesis 48:4 confirms that Abraham's promise of 'eternal possession' in the land applies to Joseph's descendants.
Leviticus 25:38 summarizes the exodus from Egypt as the fulfillment of Abraham's covenant concerning the land and God's presence.
Isaiah 60:21 confirms that Abraham's promise of eternal ownership of the land will be fully realized in the final restoration.
Ezekiel 47:14 confirms that the inheritance of the land is based on God's oath to the fathers (Abraham) in Genesis 17:8.
Ezekiel 37:27 confirms that the Abrahamic covenant formula ('I am your God') is the foundation for the future restoration.
Genesis 26:4 confirms that Abraham's promise of numerous descendants and the land remains valid for Isaac.
Ezekiel 37:25 confirms that Abraham's promise of eternal settlement in the land applies to Jacob's descendants.
Genesis 28:4 is a direct reference to Abraham's covenant in Genesis 17:8, confirmed in the blessing given to Jacob.
Genesis 35:12 confirms that Abraham's promise concerning the land remains valid for Jacob and his descendants.
Deuteronomy 4:40 expands on Abraham's promise of eternal possession by linking it to obedience to God's commands.
Numbers 33:53 is the practical fulfillment of Abraham's promise to give the land as a possession.
Leviticus 14:34 assumes that Abraham's promise to give the land as a possession has been fulfilled.
Numbers 13:2 is the first act in fulfilling Abraham's promise to give the land to the children of Israel.
Amos 9:15 confirms that Abraham's promise of eternal possession of the land will be fully realized in the final restoration.
Joshua 17:18 is a concrete realization of Abraham's promise to give the land to Israel's descendants.
Exodus 6:8 summarizes the exodus from Egypt as the fulfillment of Abraham's covenant to give the land as a possession.
Deuteronomy 11:31 is an encouragement to take possession of the land that Abraham's covenant promises.
Psalm 105:8 confirms that Abraham's covenant (regarding the land and God's presence) is an eternal covenant that God remembers.
